relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.evidence: He went to Samaldas College, Bhavnagar and completed B.A. in Sanskrit in 1939.

relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.evidence: He completed M.A. in Sanskrit and Ardhamagadhi from Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Bombay in 1941.

relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.evidence: He completed his thesis on Paumachariya, an epic poetry in Apabhramsha by Swayambhudev, and received Ph.D. under guidance of Muni Jinvijay in 1951.

relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.evidence: He was also influenced by Ralph Lilley Turner during this period.

relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.evidence: He was a professor at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan from 1945 to 1965.

relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.evidence: He returned to Ahmedabad and joined School of Languages, Gujarat University. He taught there from 1965 to 1975.

relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.evidence: He served as an honorary professor at Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology.

relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.evidence: He also served at International School of Dravidian Linguistics in 1980.

relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.object: School of Oriental and African Studies of the University of London
relations.evidence: He received honorary fellowship of the School of Oriental and African Studies of the University of London in 1993.

relations.subject: Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani
relations.evidence: In 1993, he co-founded Anusandhan, a journal featuring Jain literary works.
